title: Add JXL support via libjxl
body: ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Closes [godot-proposals/issues/13957](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13957) In short: 1. JXL offers superior compression (both lossless and lossy) over the ubiquitous JPG and PNG, which allows for smaller worktrees and smaller texture packs and panoramas when uploading to Godot asset library/store. 2. JXL is a highly flexible format supporting transparency (unlike JPG), layers (unlike JPG/PNG/WEBP), and 8/16/32 bits per channel (unlike JPG/PNG/WEBP). 3. JXL offers **much** better compression (lossless and lossy) over EXR/HDRI for 32 bit panoramas, and these files tend to be huge. 4. JXL is now supported by most major image editors (Photoshop/Gimp/Krita) which is all that's needed for it to be useful on the import side. ## Additional information A first pass at JXL implementation for Godot. I've only implemented import support in this pass to keep things simple (and due to questionable usefulness of being able to export JXLs). Notes: 1. Created a rudimentary JXL module a la WEBP module. 2. Trimmed thirdparty/libjxl down to the minimum set of files needed to build the module (+ license-related files). 3. Images with layers get squashed on import (default behavior from libjxl). Images with animations only take the first frame (consistent with lack of animated webp support). 4. Used the Godot engine helpers for converting srgb to linear space for 32 bit images; libjxl is supposed to have this capability built in (JxlDecoderSetOutputColorProfile), but I didn't have a lot of success with it, so I referenced what EXR import code was doing. This PR is mainly meant for reference for [godot-proposals/issues/13957](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13957); I don't claim to have done the full due diligence to make it merge-worthy. There are unit tests for every common case I could think of, and I've done a quick test with a project for importing JXL textures and panoramas: In this implementation, editor size increased ~1.2MB, while export sizes did not appreciably change in my mac .app and web exports. ## EDIT: Made some changes following feedback: - Encoding is now included with a new project setting for jxl encoding effort. - Image.save_jxl, Image.load_from_file, Image.load_jxl_from_buffer are all supported. - HDR images keep their full range when saved. - Multithreaded encoding and decoding that’s acceptably fast (a 4K 16-bit HDR sky loads in ~0.3s lossless, ~0.1s lossy on my M1 Max). - No increased (or decreased) export size or VRAM usage for default VRAM Compressed 3D Sky textures. - When lossy compression is selected for a JXL 3D Sky texture export size can be decreased at the cost of ~0.1s extra load time on my M1 Max and increased VRAM usage (for a single 4K 16-bit HDR Sky compressed at 0.7 effort: ~8 MB smaller download, ~45 MB more VRAM used than VRAM Compressed). - Dropped the brotli encoder dependency from libjxl since it's unneeded for this implementation. The JXL module adds about 1.5 MB to macOS export templates, 3.5 MB to x86-64 templates, and 0.3 MB to a Web game's download. This was achieved by trimming libjxl's generated SIMD code to just SSE4/AVX2 and NEON; the slowdown from not including AVX-512/BF16/SVE should be minimal. The `jxl_all_simd_targets=yes` build option adds back AVX-512/BF16/SVE. | Target | Without JXL | With JXL | Increase | |---|---|---|---| | macOS ARM64 release template | 55.8 MB | 57.4 MB | +1.6 MB (2.8%) | | macOS ARM64 debug template | 57.6 MB | 59.1 MB | +1.4 MB (2.4%) | | macOS ARM64 editor | 110.1 MB | 111.5 MB | +1.4 MB (1.2%) | | x86-64 release template (full LTO) | 62.0 MB | 65.5 MB | +3.6 MB (5.7%) | | Web release (Brotli, download size) | 6.70 MB | 7.03 MB | +0.33 MB (4.9%) | Disclaimer: some claude assistance in various areas, including unit testing.
